references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) ss.30, 56, 67
references.quote: At least 6 working days of annual leave a year after one full year of service; current-year leave is pro-rated on qualifying termination and accumulated leave is paid on either-party termination.

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) s.30
references.quote: At least 6 working days a year after one full year of service; unused days carry only where employer and employee agreed in advance.

description: Six paid working days a year after one year of service. At exit, carried-over untaken days are always paid at the day rate; this year's untaken days are paid in proportion to the months served only when the employer ends the employment for a reason outside s.119 (LPA ss.30, 67).

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) ss.32, 57
references.quote: Sick leave is for actual illness; wages are owed for up to 30 working days a year.

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) s.57
references.quote: Wages for sick leave up to 30 working days a year.

description: Paid sick leave: up to 30 working days a year at full pay (LPA s.57).

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) ss.32, 57
references.quote: Sick leave beyond 30 paid working days a year is unpaid.

description: Sick days beyond the 30 paid a year; unpaid (paid share 0) (LPA s.57).

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) ss.34, 57/1
references.quote: At least 3 working days a year for necessary business; wages are owed for up to 3 days.

description: Leave for necessary business: 3 working days a year at full pay (LPA ss.34, 57/1).

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) ss.33, 57
references.quote: Leave is allowed for sterilisation and the period a physician certifies, with wages.

description: Leave for sterilisation for the days a physician certifies, at full pay (LPA ss.33, 57).

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) ss.35, 58
references.quote: Leave is allowed for military inspection, call-up or training, with wages for up to 60 days a year.

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) s.58
references.quote: Wages for military service leave up to 60 days a year.

description: Leave for military call-up or training: full pay for up to 60 days a year (LPA s.58).

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) s.36
references.quote: Training or development leave is allowed under the Ministerial Regulation; the Act does not require wages.

description: Leave for training or skill development; unpaid (paid share 0) (LPA s.36).

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) s.52
references.quote: An employee under 18 may take up to 30 days a year for approved training, meetings or courses, with wages.

description: An employee under 18: up to 30 days a year for approved training, at full pay (LPA s.52).

references.title: Labour Protection Act (No. 9) B.E. 2568 s.41 para 1 and s.59
references.quote: Up to 120 days of maternity leave per pregnancy including holidays; wages for up to 60 days. In force 7 December 2025.

references.title: Labour Protection Act (No. 9) B.E. 2568 s.59
references.quote: Wages for up to 60 days of the maternity leave under s.41 para 1.

description: Maternity leave: the first 60 days of each pregnancy at full pay from the employer (LPA s.59 as amended by Act No. 9).

references.title: Labour Protection Act (No. 9) B.E. 2568 s.41; Social Security Act B.E. 2533 (1990) s.67
references.quote: 120 days of maternity leave less 60 employer-paid days; the Social Security Fund pays a maternity benefit at 50 percent of wages for 90 days.

description: Maternity leave after the 60 employer-paid days, up to 120 days in all; unpaid by the employer (paid share 0), the Social Security Fund pays its maternity benefit.

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) s.29 paras 3-4
references.quote: A traditional holiday on a weekly holiday is taken on the next working day; where the work cannot stop for one, another day off is agreed in substitution or holiday work pay is paid.

description: A paid day off agreed in substitution for a traditional holiday worked (s.29 para 4); HR grants each through a manual adjustment. The announced holidays (s.29: at least 13 a year) and their next-working-day substitutes are the entity calendar.

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) ss.5, 70
references.quote: Wages are owed for work and the paid leave the Act lists; other leave agreed with the employer is unpaid.

references.title: Labour Protection Act (No. 9) B.E. 2568 s.41 para 4 and s.59/1
references.quote: Up to 15 further consecutive days after maternity leave where the child is ill, at risk, abnormal or disabled, on a medical certificate; wages at 50 percent.

references.title: Labour Protection Act (No. 9) B.E. 2568 s.41 para 4
references.quote: Up to 15 more days after maternity leave for a child who is ill, abnormal or disabled.

description: Up to 15 days after maternity leave for a newborn who is ill or at risk, on a medical certificate; half pay (paid share 0.5) (LPA s.41 para 4, s.59/1).

references.title: Labour Protection Act (No. 9) B.E. 2568 s.41/1 and s.59/2
references.quote: Up to 15 days of leave to support a spouse who gives birth, before or within 90 days after the birth, with wages.

references.title: Labour Protection Act (No. 9) B.E. 2568 ss.41/1, 59/2
references.quote: Up to 15 days to support a spouse giving birth, taken within 90 days of the birth, on full wages.

description: Up to 15 days to help a legally married spouse who gives birth, taken before or within 90 days after the birth, at full pay (LPA ss.41/1, 59/2).

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) s.32 para 3; Workmen's Compensation Act B.E. 2537 s.18(1)
references.quote: A work injury or work illness is not sick leave; the Workmen's Compensation Fund pays 70 percent of the monthly wage while the employee cannot work.

description: Absence for a work injury or illness; unpaid by the employer (paid share 0), the Workmen's Compensation Fund pays 70% of wages (WCA s.18).

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) ss.116-117
references.quote: Suspension pending an investigation is at most 7 days and paid at not less than 50 percent of the working-day wage; a cleared employee gets the full wage plus 15 percent a year interest.

references.title: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) s.116
references.quote: A suspension order runs no more than 7 days.

description: Suspension pending a disciplinary investigation: up to 7 days at half pay (paid share 0.5) (LPA ss.116-117).
